files.backup.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
DUMP="/var/backups/campus-${STAMP}.dump"
ARCHIVE="${DUMP}.age"
BACKUP_RECIPIENT="${BACKUP_RECIPIENT:?load from the secret manager}"
BACKUP_IDENTITY="${BACKUP_IDENTITY:?load from the secret manager}"

pg_dump --format=custom --file="$DUMP" "$DATABASE_URL"
age -r "$BACKUP_RECIPIENT" --output "$ARCHIVE" "$DUMP"
sha256sum "$ARCHIVE" > "${ARCHIVE}.sha256"

aws s3 cp "$ARCHIVE" "s3://campus-backups/postgres/${STAMP}.age"
aws s3 cp "${ARCHIVE}.sha256" "s3://campus-backups/postgres/${STAMP}.age.sha256"

# Keep 30 days of local copies; the offsite bucket has its own lifecycle rule.
find /var/backups -name "campus-*.dump.age" -mtime +30 -delete

# Restore test: verify the checksum, decrypt, and read the archive in isolation.
sha256sum --check "${ARCHIVE}.sha256"
age --decrypt --identity "$BACKUP_IDENTITY" --output /tmp/restore-test.dump "$ARCHIVE"
pg_restore --list /tmp/restore-test.dump > /tmp/restore-test.list
psql "$RESTORE_DATABASE_URL" --command "CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS restore-test;"
pg_restore --dbname="$RESTORE_DATABASE_URL" --schema=restore-test /tmp/restore-test.dump
psql "$RESTORE_DATABASE_URL" --command "DROP SCHEMA restore-test CASCADE;"
rm -f "$DUMP" /tmp/restore-test.dump
